question_text: A group of researchers wish to develop a clinical trial assessing the efficacy of a specific medication on the urinary excretion of amphetamines in intoxicated patients. They recruit 50 patients for the treatment arm and 50 patients for the control arm of the study. Demographics are fairly balanced between the two groups. The primary end points include (1) time to recovery of mental status, (2) baseline heart rate, (3) urinary pH, and (4) specific gravity. Which medication should they use in order to achieve a statistically significant result positively favoring the intervention?
